review.summary:
Shell-correctness review of <REPO>/cloud/gcp/kernel_guest.sh (bash 5.2, set -u, no set -e). No blocker found: I could not find a quoting, exit-status, unset-variable or heredoc error that would make the paid run fail or give a wrong result. Four defects, ranked by cost: one that can idle the whole 15-hour machine (low probability), two smaller hang/waste hazards, one pair of facts whose values are not what their names say.

What I ran (stand-ins only, nothing from the repo executed, nothing touched the cloud; local bash is 3.2 and GNU coreutils 9.x g-tools, so bash-5.2-only behaviour is reasoned, not run):
- <SCRATCH>/review_shell/tests/t1_kcmd.sh : kcmd extracted verbatim, each call site run against argv printers. Final command lines are as intended, e.g. con-ron receives exactly [--jobs=32][--progress=10%][--compare][--][challenge][solution]; lake receives [comparator][--config][rh.json][--challenge-from-export][..][--solution-from-export][..] with MIMALLOC_GENERIC_COLLECT and COMPARATOR_BWRAP as two separate environment entries; an empty 4th argument adds nothing.
- <SCRATCH>/review_shell/tests/t2_loop.sh : lines 175-191 and 451-524 extracted verbatim and run with fake checkers, a fake /proc and short sleeps, in six scenarios (normal, kernel without the setting, comparator ends early, deadline, not enough memory, empty environment). launch/running/ended, the paranoid decision, the untuned kill path and the summary all behaved as the comments say.
- <SCRATCH>/review_shell/tests/t3_vars.py : every variable read in the script is assigned before any path that reads it (no set -u exit, which would be expensive here because the heartbeat subshell would outlive the main shell).
- <SCRATCH>/review_shell/tests/t4_traps.sh : the TERM trap does not fire in "( ... ) &" subshells; kill "$HB_PID" ends the heartbeat at once; globals set inside t_step persist, those set inside the background con-ron subshell do not leak.
- curl 8.5.0 src/tool_operate.c fetched for reading into <SCRATCH>/review_shell/curl_src/ (defect K3).
Primary sources read for the points below: Lean v4.36.0 Check.lean/Main.lean/LeanChecker.lean and Lean's comparator-from-export test, bubblewrap v0.9.0, GNU time 1.9, nanoda main.rs/util.rs, con-ron con-ron.rs/compare.rs, the published con-ron-compare.log.

defects.scenario: The con-ron build is meant to be a step whose failure costs one checker, but the main flow waits for it with no limit other than the whole run's deadline. Inside that background step only cargo has a time limit (timeout 2400, line 267); line 265 `git clone -q https://github.com/leanprover/con-ron` and line 263 `curl ... https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y ...` have none. If either stalls on a connection that stays open but sends nothing, con_ron_build.rc never appears, and on kernel-check (deadline 900 min) the loop sleeps until 10 minutes before the deadline. Then line 451 `budget()` returns its floor of 60, so nanoda and lake comparator are each launched with `timeout -k 30 60`, end with status 124, and line 526 reports `finish DONE "all steps ran; read kernel_facts.json"`. The heartbeat (line 162) keeps uploading throughout, so the watcher's stale-heartbeat check never fires; the only sign is the status message "waiting for con-ron to finish building".
defects.consequence: About 14.8 hours of the 32-vCPU machine billed with no checker having run, and a final state of DONE. Low probability, but it is the whole run.
defects.suggested_fix: Put a time limit on the two network commands (e.g. `timeout 300 git clone ...`, `... | timeout 900 sh -s -- ...`) and bound the wait itself by a build budget rather than by the deadline, e.g. record `BUILD_T0=$(now)` when the subshell starts and loop while `[ $(( $(now) - BUILD_T0 )) -lt 3300 ]`; if it runs out, kill the build subshell's children and go on without con-ron.

defects.scenario: `-C -` does not make `--retry` resume. In curl 8.5.0 (the version Ubuntu 24.04 ships; src/tool_operate.c lines 1138-1168 and 605-613) the resume offset is taken once from the file's size when the transfer is set up, which is 0 because line 294 has just done `rm -f "$z"`; on every retry the output file is truncated back to that offset ("Throwing away N bytes") and the transfer starts again from byte 0. `--max-time 3000` applies to each attempt. The archive is 7.7 GB, so an attempt needs an average above 2.6 MB/s. If math.mit.edu serves this client more slowly than that, or drops the connection late in each attempt, no attempt can ever finish: nine attempts of up to 50 minutes each, about 7.5 hours, then `return 1` and FAIL.
defects.consequence: In the rehearsal the VM is deleted by Google at 100 minutes with nothing kept (about 0.50 USD and no diagnosis beyond solution_fetch.err). If kernel-check is ever launched while the bucket does not hold the export (rehearsal skipped or its upload failed), up to 7.5 hours of the large machine, about 15 USD, before it fails. The download speed from that host to GCP has not been measured.
defects.suggested_fix: Retry in the shell so each attempt is a new curl process, which does pick up the partial file: `for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9; do curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 100000 --speed-time 180 --max-time 3000 -o "$z" "$SOL_URL" 2>> "$PD/logs/solution_fetch.err" && break; sleep 15; done; [ -s "$z" ] || return 1` (the SHA-256 check that follows already guards a wrongly resumed file), and stop retrying when `left` is short.

defects.scenario: This line and line 214 (`/opt/elan/bin/elan toolchain install "$KERNEL_TC"`) run in the main flow as root with no time limit. The guest's own deadline (line 160) only does `pkill -KILL -u chk`, so it cannot stop a root process, and the heartbeat (line 162) is a separate subshell that keeps reporting whatever the main flow is doing. If either download stalls on an open connection, the script sits in phase "setup" until Google deletes the VM at its maximum run time (16 h for kernel-check); the watcher sees fresh heartbeats and does nothing. The same two lines are in export_guest.sh and have worked once, so this is a low-probability hazard carried over, but here the exposure is 16 hours rather than 5.
defects.consequence: Up to 16 hours of the large machine (about 32 USD) with no result, unless a person reads the status and tears down.
defects.suggested_fix: `... | timeout 600 sh -s -- -y ...` and `timeout 1200 /opt/elan/bin/elan toolchain install ...`; t_step then fails the run in minutes instead of hanging.

defects.scenario: con-ron --compare prints one summary line that itself contains the phrase ("con-ron: accepted 51692 declarations, 5 axioms justified by the solution solution.ndjson (...)", compare.rs line 307) and then one line per theorem (line 316). `grep -c` therefore counts 6 for the 5 theorems: run on the published con-ron-compare.log it prints 6, and my stand-in run of this exact line recorded `con_ron_theorems_justified 6`. Line 523 has the same kind of slip: `fact comparator_sandbox_calls "$(wc -l < "$XC/bwrap_calls.log" ...)"` counts every line of a log that the three smoke runs have already written to (4 + 0 + 1 calls), so the real run's single sandbox call is recorded as 6.
defects.consequence: kernel_facts.json, which is the record of the run, says 6 theorems justified and 6 sandbox calls where the truth is 5 and 1. No money lost, but a wrong number in a published record.
defects.suggested_fix: Line 517: `grep -c '^con-ron: theorem .* justified by the solution$'` (or take the number from the accept line). Line 523: note `wc -l` of the log before `launch comparator` and record the difference, or name the fact for what it is.

doubts: The path that decides the paranoid kernel is first exercised on the paid run. Lines 475-477 find lake's kernel with `pgrep -u chk -x leanchecker` and read /proc/PID/environ while that process is inside bwrap's user and PID namespaces (Check.lean passes --unshare-all). The rehearsal's probe (lines 402-405) runs against a leanchecker started directly by kcmd, not through bwrap, and in the rehearsal's kernels phase lake's kernel on the three-line pair lives well under the 30-second poll, so nothing sandboxed is ever probed. By my reading it works: root in the initial namespaces sees the process under chk's uid (bwrap v0.9.0 maps the real uid to itself, line 2797) and has CAP_SYS_PTRACE over child user namespaces, and the environment is never empty (lake sets LEAN_ABORT_ON_PANIC and HOME, bwrap sets PWD), so env_readable cannot stick. What would settle it before paying: in the rehearsal, add a stand-in external kernel to tiny.json that sleeps ~90 s, and have the probe find it by name and read its environment through the sandbox.

Line 141 (`systemctl poweroff || poweroff -f`) contradicts the launcher's stated safety design at pilot_local.sh lines 46-47 ("the guest never powers itself off, so that deletion stays armed"). As I understand Compute Engine, --max-run-duration with termination action DELETE acts on a running VM; a VM the guest has stopped stays TERMINATED with its 50 GB and 200 GB hyperdisks (and their provisioned IOPS/throughput) billing until `teardown` is run, and the ledger row stays open. The script header acknowledges the disks stay. Whether that trade (save at most the hours left to the 16 h limit; pay roughly 1-1.5 USD a day until someone tears down) is wanted is the owner's call; the GCE documentation on run-duration limits for stopped VMs, or one unwatched rehearsal, would settle the behaviour.

A killed kernel reads as a rejection in the facts. Check.lean lines 444-447 print "Lean default kernel rejected the solution" for any non-zero exit, including 137 from the OOM killer, and lake then exits 1. Lines 521-522 would record comparator_lean_kernel_accepts=false and comparator_exit_status=1 with no fact that says why; only comparator.err ("Lean default exited with 137") tells the two apart. Recording `grep oom_kill /proc/vmstat` and whether comparator.err contains "exited with 137" as facts would remove the ambiguity. This matters because the script deliberately runs lake's parent (unknown size), the default kernel (82.6 GiB) and the paranoid kernel (98.8 GiB) on 251 GiB plus swap.

All stand-in tests ran under bash 3.2 with GNU coreutils 9.x g-tools on macOS; bash 5.2 itself was not available. I found no construct whose behaviour differs between the two in a way that matters here (indirect expansion, local, process substitution, heredocs in functions, empty arrays in the wrapper which has no set -u), but that is by reading.
K2's cost depends on a number nobody has measured: the download rate from math.mit.edu to a GCP VM. A range request for the first 200 MB from any GCP machine would settle it.
checked_and_fine: kcmd (line 175): each call site's final command line written out and run against argv printers (nanoda, con-ron with `--progress=10% --compare -- a b`, lake comparator, paranoid, smoke con-ron). `%` and `--` pass through bash -c untouched; unquoted $4 splits into exactly the intended environment entries and vanishes when empty; GNU time and timeout both stop option parsing at the first non-option (time.c getopt string "+af:o:pqvV"), so the checker's own options are not eaten.

Exit statuses: GNU time 1.9 exits with the command's status or 128+signal; timeout returns 124 on expiry and re-raises a child's fatal signal (checked with gtimeout: 137, 7, 124); runk returns kcmd's status after the two fact calls; `runk ...` followed on the next line by `if [ "$?" = 1 ] && cat .out .err | grep -q 'do not match'` tests runk's status and grep's, and matches lake's exit 1 plus "Challenge and solution theorem statement do not match" (Compare.lean line 85, Check.lean lines 745-747).
`r=$(set -o pipefail; zstd ... | python3 hc.py ...) || { ...; return 1; }` with `local r` declared separately: pipefail stays inside the substitution and the assignment carries its status.

set -u: every variable read is assigned first on every path (t3_vars.py plus reading), including HB_PID guarded as ${HB_PID:-} in finish, KTC/HC initialised empty at line 81, the locals in runk/launch/smoke_challenge, and `${!v}` in the G_CMP:name loop. No runtime arithmetic-expansion error is reachable (the .started files are written synchronously before any read).

Background jobs: `HB_PID=$!` and `pp=$!` are taken on the same line as their `&`; the TERM/INT trap is reset in `( ... ) &` subshells so finish cannot run twice or in a child; `wait "$pp"` waits only for the probe; no bare `wait`; the launch subshells are tracked by .rc files written with tmp+mv; the con-ron subshell's cd and exports do not leak into the main shell while s_users/s_toolchain's HC and KTC do persist because t_step calls them in the current shell.

Main loop and paranoid decision (lines 459-502), run in six stand-in scenarios: paranoid starts only after nanoda and con-ron have ended, the kernel is seen and has the setting, and both memory tests pass; the untuned path needs four sightings before `pkill -KILL -x leanchecker` then `pkill -TERM -x lake`; an early comparator exit, the deadline file and insufficient memory each give the fact and message the comments describe.

pgrep and the 15-character comm limit: `-x leanchecker` cannot match leanchecker-paranoid, whose comm is "leanchecker-par"; lake's default kernel is run as <bindir>/leanchecker (Check.lean lines 459-461, 618), and rh.json has no external kernels, so it is the only process of that name when the loop looks.

The wrapper and its heredoc: `<<'SH'` is quoted so nothing expands at write time; the single __LOG__ is filled by sed with a path containing no `|` or `&`; lake runs it as `env -i <wrapper> ...` (Check.lean lines 215-218) and it uses only absolute paths; lake's argument list always ends `-- cmd args` (line 201) so the --setenv lands after --clearenv, and bwrap applies both in order while parsing (bubblewrap.c lines 2295-2304). envprobe.sh's printf has no `%`.

The python heredocs (`python3 - args <<'PY'` in status, write_facts, nanoda_config, comparator_config): quoted delimiters, arguments arrive as sys.argv[1:], closing brace placement is valid; config keys match nanoda's Config struct and lake's Config (enable_nanoda, external_kernels).
Glob loops with no match (sync_small, the final gzip loop): the literal pattern fails `[ -f ]` and is skipped; basenames uploaded to logs/ do not collide.
`exec > >(tee -a ...) 2>&1`: the script never exits (it idles, then powers off), so nothing waits on the tee pipe; background children holding it open is harmless.

Arithmetic: swap count SWAP_GB*64 blocks of 16M is SWAP_GB GiB; the memory test 86637124+103614080+6291456 = 196,542,660 kB against MemTotal (about 263 M kB on this machine type, from the earlier run's env.txt) and against MemTotal + 0.9*SwapTotal behaves as intended; empty mt/st/prss evaluate to 0 rather than erroring.

con-ron: no rust-toolchain pin, dependencies are cc/libc/mimalloc only (build-essential suffices), `--help` exits 0, `--jobs=N`, `--progress=10%`, `--compare`, `--` and `--verified` are all accepted by the parser at the pinned commit.

pilot_local.sh diff: bash-3.2 safe (no bash-4 syntax); the hash extraction dies before anything is created if export_facts.json is not a DONE run with both matches; metadata values contain no commas or spaces; kernel-check* is added to the watch trap and the heartbeat check, and the guest does upload a heartbeat every minute.

verification.overall:
Second pass on the shell lens of <REPO>/cloud/gcp/kernel_guest.sh. All four reported defects are real in the code as written, but none is a blocker and I rate all four minor; K3 holds for line 213 only. I found one defect the first reviewer missed that I rate major (N1), and I settled doubt 2 from Google's own documentation (N2).

Ranked by what it would cost:
1. N1 (new, major, needs an OOM kill to trigger): line 45 `tee` without `-p`. If the kernel OOM-kills any process of the run, systemd stops the startup-script unit by ending only Google's script runner. The script's output pipe then has no reader and the main script is killed by SIGPIPE at its next `say`. Nothing is finished or reported and the VM bills to the 16 h limit. One-flag fix.
2. K1 (minor): the wait for the con-ron build is bounded only by the run's deadline. Low probability, but it costs the whole run and ends in DONE.
3. K3 (minor): line 213 only. Line 214 is refuted: elan aborts a stalled download itself.
4. K2 (minor): `--retry` with `-C -` restarts from byte 0 (curl 8.5.0 source, and reproduced). The "can never finish" case is unlikely: I measured 11.9 MB/s from this Mac against the 2.6 MB/s needed. On the failure path the progress meter can also kill the script's reporting, so the fix uses `-sS`.
5. N2 (new, minor, money): the self-poweroff on line 141 clears Google's termination timestamp, so the header's "Google deletes it at its maximum run time whatever happens" is false after it.
6. K4 (minor): two facts record 6 where the truth is 5 and 1.

The first reviewer's suggested fix for K1 and K3 (`... | timeout N sh -s`) does not bound a stalled curl: bash waits for every member of a pipeline (tested: `sleep 4 | gtimeout 1 sh -c cat` takes 4 s). The curl needs its own `--max-time`; my replacement lines have both.

Not verified: no bash 5.2 and no Linux here. Tests ran under bash 3.2 with GNU coreutils 9.x g-tools and curl 8.7.1. N1's chain is read from primary sources and its last two links were reproduced with stand-ins, but it was never observed on a real VM. All replacement lines were applied to a copy and pass `bash -n`. Nothing under the repository was changed, and nothing touched the cloud or the bucket.

Outside the listed sources I made read-only fetches into the directories below: the GCE run-time-limit doc page, the guest-agent unit file and runner sources, four systemd v255 source files, and a 12-second range read of the published export for the rate sample.

Files are in <SCRATCH>/verify_shell/:
- k2/srv.py, k2/req.log, k2/a.err (curl retry and resume test)
- n1/driver.sh, n1/script.sh, n1/runner.py (runner-death test)
- guest_agent/ (unit file, both runner sources, systemd v255 service.c, unit.c, cgroup.c, manager.c)
- gce_doc/limit-vm-runtime.html
- patch/apply.py, patch/kernel_guest_patched.sh, patch/t_small.sh

verdicts.evidence: Line 423 `while [ ! -e "$PD/run/con_ron_build.rc" ] && [ "$(left)" -gt 600 ]; do sleep 5; done` has no bound but the deadline. In s_conron only cargo is timed (line 267). Line 263 (`curl ... https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s`) and line 265 (`git clone -q`) carry no time limit, and git sets no low-speed limit by default. If either stalls, the rc file never appears and the loop runs until left<=600. Then budget() (line 451) returns 60, nanoda and lake comparator get `timeout -k 30 60`, and line 526 reports DONE. The heartbeat subshell (line 162) is independent, so the watcher's stale check never fires. I traced this path line by line and it is as reported. I rate it minor, not major, because it needs a connection that stays open and sends nothing during a small GitHub or rustup download; if it happens it costs the whole run (about 15 h). The reviewer's suggested `| timeout 900 sh -s` alone would not help for a stalled curl: bash waits for all pipeline members (tested: `sleep 4 | gtimeout 1 sh -c 'cat >/dev/null'` returned after 4 s, status 124).
verdicts.minimal_fix:
Line 263, replace the start with: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf --max-time 120 https://sh.rustup.rs | timeout 900 sh -s -- -y --profile minimal --default-toolchain stable --no-modify-path > ...` (rest unchanged).
Line 265: `cd "$OPT" && timeout 600 git clone -q https://github.com/leanprover/con-ron && cd con-ron && git checkout -q "$CONRON_COMMIT" || return 1`
Line 423: `w=0; while [ ! -e "$PD/run/con_ron_build.rc" ] && [ "$w" -lt 480 ] && [ "$(left)" -gt 600 ]; do sleep 5; w=$((w + 1)); done` (at most 40 min of waiting, then the run goes on without con-ron). Applied to a copy: `bash -n` passes; the capped loop was run with stand-ins.

verdicts.evidence:
The mechanism is confirmed twice. (1) curl 8.5.0 src/tool_operate.c: the resume offset is read once at set-up (lines 1138-1148, `config->resume_from = fileinfo.st_size` or 0), and on a retry the file is truncated to `outs->init` (lines 604-613, "Throwing away ... bytes"). (2) Stand-in test with curl 8.7.1 against a local server that stalls after 1 MB of 3 MB: the script's form (`--retry 4 --retry-all-errors -C -`) sent five requests, none with a Range header, and ended with exit 28 and a 1 MB file. A shell loop of separate `curl -C -` calls sent Range=None, bytes=1000000-, bytes=2000000- and produced an identical file; one more call on the complete file got 416 and exit 0.

So `-C -` does nothing here: every retry starts at byte 0 and `--max-time 3000` applies per attempt.

The worst case (no attempt can finish, 9 x 50 min) needs under 2.57 MB/s for the 7,699,933,588-byte file. I measured 143 MB in 12 s (11.9 MB/s, HTTP 206) from this Mac, so that case is unlikely. What remains is that any drop or 3-minute stall costs a full restart of about 11 minutes.

An aggravation the reviewer did not see: without `-s`, curl writes its progress meter to solution_fetch.err as one line separated by carriage returns, 79 bytes per second (measured: 2449 bytes per 30 s attempt). `tail -3` on line 296 prints the last attempt's line to stdout. Past about 830 s that line exceeds 64 KiB, the script runner's line scanner gives up and closes the pipe (see N1), and `finish FAIL` then dies at its first `say`. The failure would never be reported and the VM would bill to Google's limit.
verdicts.minimal_fix:
Replace line 296 with:
    local i got=0
    for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9; do
      curl -sSfL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 100000 --speed-time 180 --max-time 3000 -o "$z" "$SOL_URL" 2>> "$PD/logs/solution_fetch.err" && { got=1; break; }
      [ "$(left)" -gt 1200 ] || break; sleep 15
    done
    [ "$got" = 1 ] || { tail -3 "$PD/logs/solution_fetch.err"; return 1; }
Each attempt is a new curl, so `-C -` resumes from the partial file. `-sS` drops the progress meter. The enforced SHA-256 of the unpacked export (line 309) still guards a bad resume. `bash -n` passes on the patched copy.

verdicts.evidence:
Real for line 213, refuted for line 214.

Line 213: the outer `curl -sSf .../elan-init.sh` has no time limit, and elan-init.sh's own download (`ensure curl -sSfL "$ELAN_UPDATE_ROOT/latest/download/elan-$_arch.tar.gz"`, elan-init.sh lines 102-106) has none either. s_toolchain runs in the main flow as root, the deadline subshell (line 160) only does `pkill -KILL -u chk`, and the heartbeat is a separate subshell. A stall there would sit in phase "setup" until Google's limit, as reported.

Line 214: `elan toolchain install` downloads through elan's own curl backend, which sets a 30 s connect timeout and aborts below 10 bytes/s for 30 s (elan 4.4.0, src/download/src/lib.rs lines 181-191). The reported scenario, a connection that stays open and sends nothing, ends there after 30 s with an error, and t_step fails the run in minutes.

The exposure is two small GitHub downloads, the same lines that have run in export_guest.sh. As for K1, `| timeout 600 sh -s` alone does not bound a stalled outer curl.
verdicts.minimal_fix:
Line 213: `curl -sSf --max-time 120 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leanprover/elan/master/elan-init.sh | timeout 600 sh -s -- -y --no-modify-path --default-toolchain none > "$PD/logs/kernel_toolchain.log" 2>&1 || { tail -3 "$PD/logs/kernel_toolchain.log"; return 1; }`
Optional, line 214: prefix with `timeout 1800`.

verdicts.evidence:
Line 517: con-ron prints both the summary line and the per-theorem lines to stdout (con-ron at 3f22699b, crates/con-ron/src/compare.rs lines 306-316, both `println!`). The summary line itself contains "justified by the solution" followed by the file name. On the published con-ron-compare.log, `grep -c 'justified by the solution'` gives 6 for 5 theorems.

Line 523: `wc -l` of bwrap_calls.log counts the smoke tests' calls too. By Check.lean, tiny.json makes 4 sandboxed kernel runs (three external kernels plus Lean's own, runKernels lines 464-472). The wrong pair makes 0, because verifyCompare throws before runKernels. tiny_plain.json makes 1. The real run adds 1, so the fact reads 6.

No money is lost, but kernel_facts.json would carry two wrong numbers.
verdicts.minimal_fix:
Line 517: `fact con_ron_theorems_justified "$(grep -c 'justified by the solution$' "$PD/logs/con_ron.out")"` (gives 5 on the published log; the summary line does not end there).
Before line 454 add: `BW0=$(wc -l < "$XC/bwrap_calls.log" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)`
Line 523: `fact comparator_sandbox_calls "$(( $(wc -l < "$XC/bwrap_calls.log" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) - BW0 ))"`
Run with stand-ins: as written 6, proposed 1. `bash -n` passes.

new_defects.scenario:
Trigger: the Linux OOM killer kills any one process of the run during the kernels phase, for example nanoda at 85 GiB or the paranoid kernel at 99 GiB. This is the case the swap cushion, the memory test on line 482 and the first reviewer's doubt 3 are about, and the script means it to cost one checker.

What follows, read from primary sources:
- Every process of the run is in the cgroup of google-startup-scripts.service. /etc/pam.d/runuser has no pam_systemd as I recall it (not checked on the image), and bwrap does not move cgroups.
- That unit is Type=oneshot with KillMode=process and no OOMPolicy (unit file in both guest-agent repositories).
- systemd 255's default is OOMPolicy=stop (manager.c:4975, service.c:842-843). It watches memory.events of the unit (cgroup.c:2389-2407).
- For a oneshot still in SERVICE_START it calls service_enter_signal(STOP_SIGTERM) (service.c:3659-3671), which with KillMode=process signals only the main process (unit.c:4855-4893). That process is Google's script runner.
- Neither runner version handles SIGTERM (legacy google_metadata_script_runner/main.go; new cmd/gce_metadata_script_runner/scriptrunner.go uses context.Background() and no signal.Notify), so it exits. It was the only reader of the pipe that is tee's stdout.

From then on the next line printed kills tee with SIGPIPE, and the main script's next `say` or `fact` kills the main script. If the kill came before the paranoid decision, the script dies at the second `fact` on line 480, before line 483 launches the paranoid kernel.

What survives: the heartbeat subshell (prints nothing), the launch subshells and the running checkers.

Result: no final facts, kernel_facts.json stays at "smoke tests done", status stays RUNNING, and the heartbeat stays fresh so `watch` keeps waiting. The VM bills to Google's limit at 16 h, about 4-5 h more than a normal run. If the paranoid kernel was never started, getting its result needs another run of about 11 h. Raw logs and .time files still reach the bucket through sync_small.

Stand-in test (verify_shell/n1/driver.sh, bash 3.2, GNU tee 9.x; the runner stand-in pipes the script's output and receives SIGTERM after 3 s): as written, the main script reached event 3 of 8 and was gone, never finishing, while its heartbeat subshell kept writing. With `tee -p` it finished all 8.

Second trigger, same mechanism: both runners read the script's output with bufio.NewScanner at its default 64 KiB line limit and close the pipe when a line is longer (legacy main.go runCmd; new internal/run/run.go scanPipe). Line 296's `tail -3` can print such a line after a failed download (see K2).

Confidence: the chain after an OOM kill is likely (three links from source, two reproduced with stand-ins, none seen on a real VM). The OOM kill itself is possible, not expected: the published peaks fit in 251 GiB plus swap, but the size of lake's own process is unknown.
new_defects.minimal_fix:
Line 45: `exec > >(tee -p -a "$PD/pilot.log") 2>&1`
With -p (coreutils 8.24 or later; Ubuntu 24.04 has 9.4) GNU tee ignores SIGPIPE and keeps writing the file when its stdout pipe breaks, so the script's own stdout never loses its reader. `bash -n` passes on the patched copy.

new_defects.code: if [ "$n" -ge "$POWEROFF_MIN" ]; then say "nobody has deleted this machine in $POWEROFF_MIN minutes: powering off"; gcs_put "$PD/pilot.log" "$RES/pilot.log"; sync; systemctl poweroff || poweroff -f; sleep 900; fi
new_defects.scenario:
This is the first reviewer's doubt 2, now settled from Google's documentation.

Scenario: `watch` is not running when the guest reports its final state, for example the Mac is asleep or offline at the end of an 11-15 h run, for 20 minutes or more. The guest powers itself off.

Google's page "Limit the run time of a VM" says: "Stop or suspend the VM: if you or Compute Engine stop or suspend the VM, then Compute Engine releases the VM's compute resources back to the zone and clears the termination timestamp." A new timestamp is set only when the VM enters RUNNING again. The page does not name a guest-initiated shutdown; I am taking it to count as a stop (the VM ends TERMINATED either way). On that reading a powered-off VM is never deleted by --max-run-duration.

The 50 GB boot disk and the 200 GB data hyperdisk (6000 IOPS and 300 MB/s provisioned) then bill until someone runs `watch` or `teardown`, and the ledger row stays open. My estimate from list prices is 1 to 1.5 USD a day; I did not verify the prices.

The header (lines 39-41) says "the machine powers itself off, and Google deletes it at its maximum run time whatever happens", and pilot_local.sh lines 46-47 say the guest never powers itself off so that deletion stays armed. Both are untrue for this guest once line 141 has run.

The poweroff does save money in that same scenario: it stops about 2 USD/h for the hours left to the limit, and `watch` tears down a TERMINATED VM as soon as it is run again. So this is a trade-off for the owner; the defect is that the code and the two comments disagree about the backstop.
new_defects.minimal_fix: Owner's choice. Either delete the `systemctl poweroff || poweroff -f; sleep 900` part of line 141 and its `say`, which keeps Google's deletion armed and costs at most the hours left to the limit. Or keep it and correct lines 39-41 and pilot_local.sh lines 46-47 to say that after a self-poweroff nothing is deleted until `watch` or `teardown` is run.

doubts_resolved.doubt: The path that decides the paranoid kernel (pgrep for lake's kernel, reading /proc/PID/environ through bwrap's namespaces) is first exercised on the paid run.
doubts_resolved.answer: Not settled by a test: there is no Linux here. By reading it works, and the costly way for it to go wrong is not reachable. If the kernel were not found or its environment could not be read, the result would be that the paranoid kernel is never started; a correctly tuned kernel would not be killed. It is still true that the rehearsal never probes a sandboxed process. The reviewer's suggestion of a slow stand-in kernel in the rehearsal would settle it; the stand-in must be a file named `leanchecker` for pgrep to find it.
doubts_resolved.evidence: bubblewrap.c: `if (opt_sandbox_uid == -1) opt_sandbox_uid = real_uid;`, so the host sees the sandboxed process under chk's uid. bwrap does `xsetenv ("PWD", ...)`, and Check.lean lines 186-190 and 436-437 add LEAN_ABORT_ON_PANIC and HOME, so the environment is never empty. doubts_resolved.doubt: Line 141 powers the machine off, against the launcher's stated design; does Google's deletion at the maximum run time still apply to a stopped VM?
doubts_resolved.answer: Settled, on one reading: no. A stopped VM loses its termination timestamp and is not deleted at the maximum run time; its disks bill until `watch` or `teardown` is run. review.summary:
Lens: will each tool run as invoked. I read <REPO>/cloud/gcp/kernel_guest.sh, the pilot_local.sh diff and export_guest.sh against the fetched sources (Lean v4.36.0 Check.lean/Main.lean/InstallPath.lean/Env.lean/LeanChecker.lean/LeanExport, nanoda 4c544ed4, con-ron 3f22699b, bubblewrap 0.9.0, GNU time 1.9) and fetched curl 8.5.0's tool_operate.c into <SCRATCH>/review_toolrun/curl_8_5_0/. Nothing was built or run beyond bash -n and grep.

No blocker found. The central invocation (`lake comparator` as chk through the bwrap wrapper, from a directory with no lakefile) matches the source on every point I could check: install detection, config keys, kernel order, sandbox argv, output lines and exit codes. The published robin1984 log shows the same code path finishing under real bwrap on Ubuntu.

Five defects, ranked by cost:
1. Line 423 waits for the con-ron build (a "soft" step) until 10 minutes before the deadline. Only `cargo build` has a time limit, so a stalled rustup or git fetch would idle the whole paid run. Unlikely, but it costs everything.
2. The rehearsal runs con-ron in plain mode on the challenge export, which uses sorryAx. con-ron declines that with exit 2, so the rehearsal reports a con-ron failure and never tries the real `--compare --` form.
3. The public download cannot resume: in curl 8.5 `-C -` does nothing across `--retry`; each retry restarts 7.7 GB from zero under a 50-minute cap.
4. GNU time's figures for `lake comparator` exclude the sandboxed kernel, because bwrap's monitor exits without reaping the sandbox's pid 1. `comparator_max_rss_kb` will be lake's own peak only.
5. `con_ron_theorems_justified` will read 6, not 5, and `comparator_sandbox_calls` includes the smoke tests' calls.

The rehearsal settles most of the remaining unknowns (sandbox on this image, cargo build, tiny exports). It does not exercise finding the sandboxed kernel and starting the paranoid kernel; that logic first runs in the paid run.

defects.scenario: The con-ron build runs in the background as a soft step (line 278). Inside s_conron only `cargo build` has a limit (`timeout 2400`, line 267). The rustup install (line 263, `curl ... | sh`) and `git clone` (line 265) have none. If either stalls at application level, con_ron_build.rc never appears. The main script then sits at line 423 until `left` is 600 s, i.e. about 14 h 50 min into a 15 h run. The heartbeat comes from a separate subshell (line 162), so the watcher sees a healthy guest.
defects.consequence: nanoda, `lake comparator` and the paranoid kernel are not started until 10 minutes before the deadline. They are then launched with `budget` = 60 s and killed. The whole paid run (about 15 h of the 32-vCPU machine) produces nothing. The trigger is improbable; the wait itself is certain from the code. In the ordinary case the same line only delays the 10-hour critical path by whatever remains of a single-threaded fat-LTO build (119k lines, codegen-units=1), probably a few minutes. The same class exists at line 213 (elan-init and `elan toolchain install` without time limits inside a hard t_step), inherited from export_guest.sh.
defects.suggested_fix: Do not put the long checkers behind the con-ron build. Either bound the wait by its own clock (e.g. 30 min from when the build started), or launch nanoda and the comparator first and start con-ron from the monitor loop when con_ron_build.rc appears. Also wrap the whole of s_conron in `timeout`, and give the rustup/elan curl calls `--max-time`.

defects.scenario: In the rehearsal SOLX is the challenge export, whose five theorems are `by sorry`. con-ron in plain mode tolerates the sorryAx declaration but declines any use of it: unknown_const_error / unresolved_consts_error return NotImplemented ("use of the sorryAx axiom"), which the CLI maps to exit 2 (con-ron-core/src/arena/core.rs:746-756, checker_base.rs:528-551). The script already allows sorryAx for nanoda in the rehearsal (line 438) but con-ron has no such switch.
defects.consequence: Every rehearsal will record con_ron_exit_status=2, an empty con_ron_accept_line and zero justified theorems, which reads as a con-ron failure. The form the paid run uses (line 446, `--jobs=N --progress=10% --compare -- CHALLENGE SOLUTION`) is never executed before the paid run; the small smoke test also uses plain mode. That form is accepted by the parser at 3f22699b (con-ron.rs:269-306, 909-917), so this is a rehearsal that cannot show what it is meant to show, not a predicted failure of the paid run.
defects.suggested_fix: In the rehearsal, run the real form on the tiny pair: RON_ARGS="--jobs=$NMAX --progress=10% --compare -- $XT/Challenge.export $XT/Solution.export". Expected: exit 0, an accept line with "1 axioms justified", and one "theorem comm justified by the solution" line.

defects.scenario: In curl 8.5.0 (Ubuntu 24.04) `-C -` fixes the resume offset once, from the file size when the transfer is set up (tool_operate.c:1138-1168); here that is 0 because of the `rm -f` just before. On every retry curl prints "Throwing away N bytes" and truncates the file back to that initial offset (tool_operate.c:604-632). So a dropped connection at 6 GB of the 7,699,933,588-byte file restarts from zero. `--max-time 3000` applies to each attempt, so any sustained rate below about 2.6 MB/s can never finish: every attempt times out at 50 min, is retried by --retry-all-errors and starts over.
defects.consequence: On a flaky or slow link from math.mit.edu, up to 9 attempts of 50 min each (7.5 h) with nothing kept. This curl runs as root in a foreground t_step, so the guest's own deadline does not stop it. In the rehearsal the loss is capped by the 100-minute maximum run time. In the paid run it only bites if the bucket copy is missing or its fetch failed (line 293 treats any gcs_get failure as "not in the bucket").
defects.suggested_fix: Make the retry a shell loop so that each new curl invocation resumes: for i in 1..8; do curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 100000 --speed-time 180 -o "$z" "$SOL_URL" && break; sleep 15; done. Drop --retry and --max-time from the inner call and bound the loop by wall clock instead. The server honoured Range requests during the research.

defects.scenario: For l=comparator the .time file comes from `time -v timeout lake comparator`. GNU time reports getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN), which only includes descendants that were waited for. With --unshare-all bwrap creates an eventfd (bubblewrap.c 0.9.0:2832-2834). Its monitor returns as soon as it reads the exit code from that eventfd (lines 546-554) and main returns that value (line 2989) without ever reaping the sandbox's pid 1. The kernel's CPU time and peak RSS therefore never reach lake, timeout or time. The published robin1984-lake-comparator-4.36.log shows exactly this: 43.57 s user time and 0% CPU over 3 h 51 min, max RSS 2.0 GB.
defects.consequence: comparator_max_rss_kb (and the CPU lines copied into comparator.time.txt at line 508) describe the lake process alone, not the Lean kernel it ran in the sandbox. On the proof that will be lake's own parse peak, a plausible-looking number that would be read as the kernel's memory. The sandboxed kernel's peak is recorded nowhere except the 5-minute `ps` samples in procs.log. No money is lost; a recorded fact is wrong.
defects.suggested_fix: Rename the fact to say it is lake's own process. Record the kernel's peak directly: the loop already has its pid (`kp`), so sample VmHWM from /proc/$kp/status each tick and report the last value as comparator_kernel_hwm_kb. Standalone runs (nanoda, con-ron, leanchecker, paranoid) are unaffected: their chain time -> timeout -> program is fully waited.

defects.scenario: con-ron's accept line itself contains the phrase: "con-ron: accepted 51692 declarations, 5 axioms justified by the solution solution.ndjson (...)" (compare.rs:306-317), followed by one line per theorem. Running the same grep -c on the published con-ron-compare.log, and on this repository's own con_leche_compare.tail.txt, gives 6.
defects.consequence: A correct run records con_ron_theorems_justified = 6 where the true number is 5. Similarly, line 523 (`wc -l < bwrap_calls.log`) counts the five sandbox calls made by the smoke tests, so comparator_sandbox_calls will read 6 for a real run that made one call. Wrong numbers in kernel_facts.json; nothing else depends on them.
defects.suggested_fix: Line 517: grep -c '^con-ron: theorem .* justified by the solution$'. Line 523: note the line count of bwrap_calls.log just before `launch comparator` and report the difference.

doubts: Sandbox preconditions on this image cannot be settled from source: whether `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` still exists under that name on kernel 7.0.0-1017-gcp (s_sysctl ignores failure and returns 0), whether the image ships an AppArmor profile for bwrap, and whether /run/user exists with no login session (I expect yes, from systemd's tmpfiles `d /run/user`). bwrap dies with "Can't mkdir" if a --tmpfs target is missing under the read-only bind. The rehearsal's smoke_comparator settles all three; read smoke_comparator_accepts_right_solution and logs/sysctl.log before paying for the long run.

Finding the sandboxed kernel is first exercised in the paid run (lines 475-484: `pgrep -u chk -x leanchecker`, then root reading /proc/PID/environ of a process inside bwrap's user and pid namespaces). The rehearsal's probe (smoke_challenge) watches an unsandboxed leanchecker, and the rehearsal's comparator runs the three-line pair, whose kernel stage lasts under a second, so the 30-second loop will always report "lake comparator ended before its kernel stage was seen". I believe the detection works: host /proc lists processes in child pid namespaces, the uid is unchanged, and init-namespace root holds CAP_SYS_PTRACE over descendant user namespaces. If it did not, the 10-hour paranoid kernel would silently never start. What would settle it: in the rehearsal, give the comparator a pair whose kernel stage lasts minutes, e.g. challenge.ndjson as both challenge and solution with sorryAx added to permitted_axioms, so the detection, the allocator check and `launch paranoid` all run once for cents.

Whether `cargo build --release` of con-ron 3f22699b compiles on today's stable Rust, and how long it takes. The record's rustc version is unpublished. The source has no #![feature], no deny(warnings), no build.rs and no rust-toolchain file; Cargo.lock v4 needs cargo 1.78 or later; libmimalloc-sys needs only cc. The rehearsal settles it (setup.tsv con_ron_build, logs/con_ron_build.log). A plain `git clone` followed by `git checkout 3f22699b` also assumes that commit is still reachable from a branch.

Whether con-ron 3f22699b and the bundled nanoda accept the tiny export of a `by grind` proof made by Lean v4.36.0. Lean's own comparator test sets enable_nanoda false, so nanoda has not been shown on that file. nanoda sits inside tiny.json, so a nanoda rejection there would fail smoke_comparator and switch off the long part (G_CMP=0) for a reason unrelated to the proof. The rehearsal shows it either way.

Whether Google Cloud Storage validates the bearer token only when a single-request upload starts. The metadata server can hand out a token with as little as about 5 minutes left. It only matters if the 7.7 GB upload takes longer than that; from a GCE VM in the same region with the file in page cache I expect 1 to 3 minutes. The documented size limit for uploadType=media is 5 TiB, so size is not a problem.
Throughput and reachability of math.mit.edu from a GCE address are unknown (the research fetched from a home connection). See D3 for what a slow link does.
checked_and_fine: lake comparator needs no lakefile or workspace in /mnt/work/cmp: Main.lean:1214-1224 does not load the workspace, and with both --*-from-export flags needsProject is false (Check.lean:725-728), so no manifest check, no resolve, no build, no .lake directory.

Lake finds its Lean install with no elan and ELAN_HOME unset: findLakeLeanJointHome? uses IO.appPath and the co-located bin/lean (InstallPath.lean), giving sysroot /opt/elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.36.0. Env.compute only reads environment variables and writes nothing under HOME or the toolchain.

COMPARATOR_BWRAP with a bash wrapper: whichExe runs `which <path>`; debianutils `which` prints an absolute path that is an executable file. Lake then spawns /usr/bin/env -i <wrapper> <bwrap args> (Check.lean:213-220). The wrapper has an absolute shebang and uses only absolute paths and builtins, so the empty PATH is harmless. It execs bwrap, so --die-with-parent still refers to lake.

The wrapper's insertion point is right: bwrap applies --clearenv and --setenv in argument order while parsing (bubblewrap.c 0.9.0:2295-2308), and lake's argv has exactly one "--", directly before the command (Check.lean:201).

Config JSON matches the Config structure (Check.lean:540-548): keys challenge_module, solution_module, theorem_names, permitted_axioms, enable_nanoda, external_kernels (the `?` is dropped from JSON keys; Lean's own test config.json and Help.lean:458-478 confirm). external_kernels as an object of arrays is the community file's shape. The two configs never combine a true enable_nanoda with external_kernels.

Kernel order and command lines in the smoke config: TreeMap order is "Lean paranoid", "envprobe", "nanoda", then the built-in "Lean default". Commands: leanchecker-paranoid --silent --from-export <export>; /opt/kernels/envprobe.sh <export>; nanoda_bin <generated config in /tmp> (name contains "noda"); leanchecker --silent --from-export <export>. "Lean paranoid" does not contain "noda".

Sandbox contents for each kernel: --ro-bind / / is recursive, so /opt/kernels, /opt/elan and /mnt/work are visible; /bin/sh exists for the envprobe shebang; the generated config (/tmp/tmp.XXXXXXXX, mode 0600, same uid) is bound back after the --tmpfs /tmp; cwd is /tmp; the network namespace is new, so the iptables rules on chk are irrelevant.

Output lines and streams: lake prints "<name> kernel accepts the solution" and "Your solution is okay!" with IO.println on stdout (so "Lean default kernel accepts the solution" appears even though leanchecker is --silent). A mismatch gives "error: Challenge and solution theorem statement do not match: 'comm'" on stderr and exit 1, with no kernel run. Exit 2 means could not start. The script's four grep patterns and its `$? = 1` test match.

Tiny project: lakefile, three .lean files, targets and commands are those of tests/lake/tests/comparator-from-export/test.sh. No dependencies, so no network. With a lean-toolchain equal to the running toolchain, Workspace.updateToolchain logs "already up-to-date" and does not restart. `lake env leanexport Mod -- targets` passes the arguments through (Main.lean:1275-1284).

nanoda config: every key the script writes exists in Config at 4c544ed4 (src/util.rs:871-933), and there is no deny_unknown_fields. With pp_to_stdout true and print_axioms defaulting to true, the admitted axioms are printed first, then "Checked N declarations with no errors" at the start of a line; that is the config and regex of Lean's tests/pkg/nanoda/run_test.sh. Accept lines are on stdout, progress and errors on stderr. Exit codes: 0 accept, 1 reject, 2 decline, 3 usage or internal. The binary is at target/release/con-ron under the workspace root; chk can execute it after chmod -R a+rX with /opt/kernels at 755.

GNU time 1.9 and timeout: both stop option parsing at the first non-option, so the "--" in con-ron's arguments reaches con-ron. gcs_get on a missing object: with -f a 404 writes no body and is not retried, and the script removes the path anyway. gcs_put of 7.7 GB: -T with a regular file sends Content-Length; the 1024 B/s for 120 s rule only trips on a real stall.

pilot_local.sh diff: bash 3.2 compatible; the python one-liner yields empty KV unless the export-check finished with both exports matching; metadata values contain no commas; instance and disk names are valid; watch treats kernel-check* like full* (heartbeat, no teardown on Ctrl-C).

verification.overall:
All five of the first reviewer's defects are real, and none is a blocker. I re-rated D1 from major to minor; the other four stay minor. I found one new minor defect (a wrong number in the facts) and no invocation that would stop a tool from running.

**How I checked.** I read <REPO>/cloud/gcp/kernel_guest.sh against the fetched sources: Lean v4.36.0 (Check.lean, Main.lean, InstallPath.lean, Env.lean, LeanChecker.lean, Compare.lean, Axioms.lean, Help.lean, Lean's own comparator and nanoda tests), nanoda 4c544ed4, con-ron 3f22699b, bubblewrap 0.9.0, GNU time 1.9, curl 8.5.0's tool_operate.c, and the published logs. I fetched three Linux v6.8 files and systemd v255's tmpfiles file into <SCRATCH>/verify_fidelity/ (src_linux, src_systemd) to settle two doubts. Small stand-in tests are in <SCRATCH>/verify_fidelity/tests/ (t_d1.sh, t_d5.sh, wrapper_test.sh, t_stage.sh, t_fixes.sh). Nothing was built, and nothing touched the cloud or the repository.

**The central path holds up.** `lake comparator` as chk through the wrapper, from a directory with no lakefile, matches the source on install detection, option parsing, config keys, kernel order, the bwrap argument list, output strings and exit codes. The wrapper, run unchanged against a stand-in bwrap that applies --clearenv/--setenv in order, leaves MIMALLOC_GENERIC_COLLECT set and logs the line the smoke test greps for. The published page shows `lake comparator` v4.36.0 reaching its kernel stages on this same pair of exports (challenge sha bd484ac9…, solution 5ea74b91…), so the statement and axiom comparison is known to pass.

**Verdicts in one line each:**
- **D1** (line 423, unbounded wait for the con-ron build): real, minor. Only a stalled rustup or git clone triggers it, but then the whole 15 h run is lost; one line fixes it.
- **D2** (rehearsal runs con-ron in plain mode on a `sorry` file): real, minor. Every rehearsal will show con-ron exit 2, and the `--compare --` form is never tried before the paid run.
- **D3** (`curl --retry` with `-C -` restarts from zero in 8.5.0): real, minor.
- **D4** (GNU time does not see the sandboxed kernel): real, minor. The published robin1984 log shows it directly: 43.57 s of user time over 3 h 51 min.
- **D5** (grep counts 6 for 5 theorems; sandbox-call count includes 5 smoke calls): real, minor. Both are reproduced on the published log.

**New defect:** `comparator_seconds_to_kernel_stage` is taken when the monitor first looks after nanoda and con-ron have ended, not when the kernel started. With the kernel at +900 s and nanoda ending at +2400 s, the script's own loop records 2400.

**What the rehearsal still cannot show:** finding the sandboxed kernel from the host and starting the paranoid kernel beside it. From kernel source this should work (root holds CAP_SYS_PTRACE over child user namespaces; the uid is unchanged), but it first runs in the paid run.

verdicts.evidence:
The code is as described. Line 278 runs s_conron in a background subshell that writes con_ron_build.rc only when s_conron returns. Inside s_conron only `cargo build` is bounded (line 267, `timeout 2400`); the rustup `curl | sh` (line 263) and `git clone` (line 265) have no limit. Line 423 then waits while the rc file is missing and `left` > 600.

Simulation of line 423 with a simulated clock (verify_fidelity/tests/t_d1.sh): with the rc file never appearing, the wait ends at minute 890 of 900 and `budget` returns 60 s, so nanoda, lake comparator and the paranoid kernel would be started and killed.

Why minor rather than major: it needs a rustup or git transfer that stalls without ever failing, which is rare (that is my estimate, not a measurement). In the ordinary case the wait costs at most the remainder of the build, probably zero to a few minutes, because the inputs phase and smoke tests run meanwhile. While waiting, the status reads 'waiting for con-ron to finish building', so a watched run would be noticed; an unattended one would lose the full 15 h.
verdicts.minimal_fix:

review.summary:
Read-only review of <REPO>/cloud/gcp/kernel_guest.sh and the uncommitted launcher changes in <REPO>/cloud/gcp/pilot_local.sh, through the lens of money, time and lost results. Nothing was run against the cloud. My stand-in tests are in <SCRATCH>/review_money/ (sim.sh replays the monitoring loop, lines 459-502 verbatim, on a virtual clock in ten scenarios).

No blocker: I found nothing that would certainly fail the long run, and no path that records a checker as accepting when it did not run or failed. The script fails cheaply in most bad cases (a comparator that dies early ends the run after about an hour).

What can cost real money, in order of expected cost:
1. The rehearsal never executes the branch that finds lake comparator's kernel and starts the paranoid kernel. That branch first runs for real on the 2 USD/h machine.
2. The 15 h deadline is tighter than the comments suggest. The earlier export-check on this same machine type ran its single-threaded export 11% slower than the published machine (5,718 s against 5,135 s). On that ratio the run is about 12.3 h (about 25 USD), not 11, and the paranoid kernel has 23% slack before its timeout kills it.
3. The wait for the con-ron build is bounded only by the deadline, so one hung download there idles the machine for 14.8 h and then gives every checker 60 s.
4. An out-of-memory kill of the kernel inside lake comparator is recorded exactly like a rejection of the proof.
5. The new self-poweroff clears Google's scheduled deletion (the repo's own README says so), so the disks bill until someone runs teardown, outside the ledger.

The rest are small: one fact is certainly wrong (con_ron_theorems_justified will read 6, not 5), a few are mislabelled, and results of the short checkers reach kernel_facts.json only at the very end.

Cap check: worst case 32.07 USD (kernel-check) and 0.52 USD (rehearsal); 46.32 + 0.52 + 32.07 = 78.91, so both launch. After one long run of about 12.3 h, a second would be refused (about 103.5 against 100), so any failure that needs a rerun also needs the cap raised.

Could a passing rehearsal be followed by a first-hour failure? Yes, from three things it does not exercise: lake comparator parsing the real 61.6 GB export in its own process (memory unknown), the kernel-detection branch, and con-ron's --compare argument form (which I checked against the source and is valid).

Cheaper way: I see none that is material. Both Lean kernels at once need about 182 GiB plus lake's parent, and at 8 GB per vCPU that forces n4d-highmem-32; two half-size machines or a sequential run cost the same or more. Starting the paranoid kernel without waiting for nanoda would save at most 20 to 50 minutes (1 to 2 USD) for a tighter memory peak. Spot is about 40% cheaper per hour, but one preemption forfeits an 11 to 12 hour run that cannot checkpoint.

defects.scenario: In the rehearsal, lake comparator runs on the three-line pair, so its kernel stage lasts well under a second. The loop first looks after `sleep 30` (line 470), and only once nanoda and con-ron have ended, so it always takes the `ended comparator` exit at line 473. Even if the kernel were seen, line 482 would refuse: DEF_PEAK_KB+PAR_PEAK_KB+MARGIN_KB is 187.4 GiB against a 32 GB machine, and the rehearsal metadata (pilot_local.sh line 1098, `MD="pilot-nmax=4,kernel-long=1,kernel-swap-gb=2"`) does not lower them. So lines 475-494 (pgrep of a process inside bwrap's user and PID namespaces, reading its environment, the memory rule, `launch paranoid`, the 4-strike kill) never run before the long run. smoke_challenge (lines 399-413) tries pgrep and the environment read only on an unsandboxed leanchecker. The header (line 36) says the rehearsal runs every step.
defects.consequence: Any fault in that branch shows up first on the 2 USD/h machine. My simulation of the case where detection never succeeds: lake comparator runs its full 9 to 10 hours, the paranoid kernel never starts, and the fact reads 'lake comparator ended before its kernel stage was seen'. The paranoid result then needs a second run of about 12 hours (about 25 USD), which the 100 USD cap would refuse. I found no actual fault in the branch by reading and simulating it; the gap itself is certain.

Untested suggestion: use the challenge export as both challenge and solution, with a config naming `riemannHypothesis` and permitting `sorryAx` beside the three standard axioms (Lean's kernel takes about 70 s on a file of that size per the community notes), and have the launcher pass small `kernel-default-peak-kb`, `kernel-paranoid-peak-kb` and `kernel-margin-kb` in the rehearsal metadata so `launch paranoid` runs on challenge.ndjson. A shorter tick in the rehearsal would make the timing safe on 4 vCPUs.

defects.scenario: The published 9 h 08 and 10 h 00 are from another machine. The only single-threaded Lean job timed on both is the export of Main: 5,718 s on this machine type (records/cloud/export-check/export-check-20261123-180914, solution_export_seconds) against 5,135 s in the published sandbox-timeline.txt, a ratio of 1.11. Scaled, the paranoid kernel needs about 11.1 h. It cannot start until nanoda ends (line 472), about 65 to 70 minutes after boot, and its timeout is `left - 600`, about 13.7 h. That is 23% slack; it is killed if this VM is more than 1.37 times slower than the published machine on that workload. Swap activity or a slow nanoda eats into the same slack. The kernels run with --silent, so nothing shows how far they got.

For example DEADLINE_MIN=1140 and MAXRUN=72000 give a worst case of 40.07 USD, and 46.32 + 0.52 + 40.07 = 86.91 still passes the 100 USD cap. Correct the 'about 11 hours' comment.

If either stalls without closing the connection, con_ron_build.rc never appears and the main script waits here until 10 minutes before the deadline, about 14.8 hours. The heartbeat keeps running, so watch sees a healthy guest. Then `budget()` (line 451) returns 60, so nanoda, con-ron and lake comparator are each launched with a 60-second timeout. The trigger is unlikely; the mechanism is plain from the code.

The only trace of the difference is 'exited with 137' in logs/comparator.err. The script saves no kernel log, so an OOM kill of nanoda, the paranoid kernel or lake's parent appears only as exit status 137, the same as other kills.

Record lake's own line as a fact (`grep -h 'exited with' comparator.err | tail -1`). Name any exit status of 128 or more as 'killed by signal N' rather than leaving it to be read as a verdict.

defects.scenario: The Mac running watch is off or has rebooted (it has before) when the guest finishes. Twenty minutes later the guest powers off. The repo's own documents say what follows: cloud/gcp/README.md ('It is cleared if the VM is stopped. For that reason the guest never powers itself off') and full_guest.sh lines 60-62 ('A guest shutdown would clear the VM's scheduled deletion'). The instance sits TERMINATED with its 50 GB and 200 GB hyperdisks (the data disk with 6000 IOPS and 300 MB/s provisioned) until someone runs watch or teardown. The header of this script (lines 39-41) says the opposite: 'Google deletes it at its maximum run time whatever happens'. The launcher's safety note (pilot_local.sh lines 46-48) is now also wrong for these modes.
defects.consequence: Disk charges with no upper bound and outside the ledger and cap; my estimate from list prices is 1 to 1.5 USD a day (unverified). The ledger is also wrong the other way: teardown closes the row at min(now - created, MAXRUN+120) at the VM rate (pilot_local.sh line 1245), so a machine that powered off after 3 hours and is torn down two days later is recorded as 32.07 USD, which can make the cap refuse the next launch. The poweroff is still the cheaper choice for an absence shorter than about a week (it saves up to 4.7 idle hours, and up to 30 USD after an early failure); the defect is the false statement and the unbounded tail.
defects.suggested_fix: Keep the poweroff, but correct the header, the README row and the launcher's safety note to say: after a self-poweroff nothing is deleted automatically, the disks bill until `teardown`, and the ledger does not count that. Consider having teardown close the row at the time of the last heartbeat for a TERMINATED instance.

defects.scenario: nanoda and con-ron end within the first hour, but their exit status, seconds and verdict lines become facts only after the loop ends, 10 or more hours later. $PD/run/*.rc is not in sync_small, and write_facts is not called between 'smoke tests done' and finish. If the run is cut in between (a teardown from the Mac, a stale-heartbeat teardown during a storage outage, a host failure), kernel_facts.json in the bucket is the pre-run version with no result for either.

defects.scenario: prss is VmRSS of lake's parent (line 189), which leaves out whatever of it was already pushed to swap during the overlap with nanoda, and st is SwapTotal, not SwapFree. A parent of 150 GiB with 40 GiB already swapped reads as 110 GiB and passes (the limit is 121.7 GiB with 64 GiB swap), though the real total, 82.6 + 98.8 + 150 GiB, exceeds memory plus swap. In the other direction, if the swap file failed to appear, a parent above 64.1 GiB skips the paranoid kernel.
defects.consequence: Only matters if lake's parent is far larger than the roughly 80 GiB I expect: the paranoid kernel is then started into memory that is not there, and hours later the OOM killer ends one of the two long kernels.
defects.suggested_fix: Use VmRSS + VmSwap for the parent and SwapFree in place of SwapTotal.

defects.scenario: nanoda (expected about 50 minutes) and con-ron (about 8) are given `left - 600`, about 14.6 hours. The paranoid kernel may start only when both have ended (line 472). If either hangs or crawls, for example nanoda's 32 threads thrashing in swap, the paranoid kernel is never started and 85 GiB stays held for the whole run.
defects.consequence: A full-length run that returns only lake comparator's result; the paranoid kernel needs a second run.
defects.suggested_fix: Cap nanoda at about 3 hours and con-ron at about 1 hour: min(budget, cap).

defects.scenario: --max-time applies to each attempt, and on a retry curl truncates the output back to where the command began (from my memory of curl 8.5's tool_operate.c, not read here), so `-C -` does not carry progress across retries. The 7.7 GB file must therefore arrive at 2.57 MB/s or better within one 50-minute attempt, or no attempt can ever succeed; nine attempts are 7.5 hours. In the rehearsal the 100-minute machine limit bounds this at about 0.50 USD but the run ends with no final status. On the long machine it applies only if the bucket copy is missing or its fetch fails.
defects.consequence: A healthy but slow download is killed and restarted from zero. Worst case on the long machine about 15 USD before `finish FAIL`.
defects.suggested_fix: Drop --max-time (the speed limit already catches a stall), or loop in the shell around a single `curl -C -` so each try resumes.

defects.scenario: Three facts are named for more than they measure. (1) comparator_seconds_to_kernel_stage is the time until nanoda and con-ron had ended and the kernel was then seen; my simulation with the kernel starting at 1,800 s records 3,000. (2) comparator_sandbox_calls (line 523) counts every line of bwrap_calls.log, including the five calls of the smoke tests, so the proof's single call reads as 6. (3) comparator_max_rss_kb (line 507) is lake's own process only: bubblewrap's outer process exits on the eventfd without reaping its child (bubblewrap.c lines 544-554), so GNU time never sees the kernel; the published Robin1984 log shows the same (43 s of user time over a 3 h 51 run). In the rehearsal paranoid_not_started_because will always read 'lake comparator ended before its kernel stage was seen' although that stage ran and accepted.
defects.consequence: Misleading entries in kernel_facts.json; no cost.
defects.suggested_fix: Rename the first to ..._when_kernel_first_seen, count only the calls logged after comparator.started for the second, and name the third comparator_parent_max_rss_kb (take the kernel's peak from procs.log).

doubts: Size of lake comparator's own process while it parses the 61.6 GB export. It uses the same parser as leanchecker, whose whole peak is 82.6 GiB, and con-ron counts 1.07 billion expression nodes, so I expect about 80 GiB, freed before the kernel stage. If that holds, the first hour peaks near 165 to 245 GiB of 251 GiB with 64 GiB swap behind it. It is unpublished; if it were above about 120 GiB the first hour would swap heavily or lose a process. The script then fails cheaply (about an hour), but with no long results. The run itself will settle it: comparator.time holds exactly this process's peak.

Whether pgrep -u chk -x leanchecker and a read of /proc/PID/environ work from root on a process inside bwrap's user and PID namespaces. I believe they do (the uid stays chk outside the namespace, and root holds CAP_SYS_PTRACE over a child namespace), but nothing before the long run tries it. The rehearsal change in the first defect would settle it for about 0.20 USD.

Whether the published 9 h 08 and 10 h 00 kernel runs were made on the same machine as the published export (EPYC 9R45). My 1.11 speed ratio rests on that; the page does not name the machine for the kernel runs. The rehearsal's smoke_leanchecker_challenge_seconds on the same CPU family gives a second, rough calibration against the community's 70 s on a 371 MB export.
Download speed from math.mit.edu to a us-central1 VM. The rehearsal needs at least 2.57 MB/s for the fetch to complete at all (see the published-copy defect). The rehearsal settles it.

My suggested rehearsal comparator (the challenge export as both sides, sorryAx permitted) is unrun. Compare.lean and Axioms.lean read as if it passes, and smoke_challenge already expects leanchecker to accept that file, but it needs one try.

If lake comparator dies before its kernel stage, the script deliberately does not run the paranoid kernel (line 473), although that kernel is standalone and would fit in memory. This is cheap (the run ends in about an hour), but if lake comparator cannot run on this machine at all, the paranoid result needs a separate launch. A design choice for the owner, not a defect.
The disk cost after a self-poweroff (1 to 1.5 USD a day) is my estimate from hyperdisk-balanced list prices as I remember them; the pricing page would settle it.

Monitoring loop, simulated in ten scenarios (normal, kernel seen late, untuned, comparator dies in seconds, nanoda and con-ron never started, large parent, no swap, slow, kernel never detected, long checkers off): it behaves as written, with no unbound variable under set -u.

The 4-strike rule cannot kill a healthy tuned kernel. A strike needs a readable environment without the variable, the environment is fixed at exec, a tuned reading leaves the waiting state at once, and the paranoid kernel's process name (leanchecker-par) does not match -x leanchecker. A process vanishing between the two reads counts as one strike, but four in a row would need the comparator to be ending anyway.

The wrapper: bubblewrap applies --clearenv and --setenv in argument order (bubblewrap.c lines 2295-2304), so the variable inserted before `--` survives. The envprobe stand-in proves this in the smoke test before anything long starts, and a failure there stops the long part.

con-ron at 3f22699b accepts `--jobs=32 --progress=10% --compare -- CHALLENGE SOLUTION` and prints its verdict lines on stdout, where the script greps. nanoda's config keys, its exit codes and the 'Checked N declarations with no errors' line match the source at 4c544ed4. The 'do not match' grep matches Lake's message.

sync_small covers every log, .time file, configuration, bwrap_calls.log, procs.log and facts.tsv. Not uploaded: the $PD/run markers, the tiny test's sources and exports, and the helper scripts, all reproducible or echoed in pilot.log. Empty files upload correctly (tested with curl against a local stand-in: Content-Length 0, exit 0).
The proof's export is put in the bucket only after the unpacked bytes hash to the expected SHA-256, under an object name that carries that hash; a mismatch ends the run.

The final status is uploaded after the facts and logs, and watch deletes only on that status. Timeouts end 10 minutes before the guest deadline, which is 59 minutes before Google's limit; finish needs about two minutes.

watch: a final status or a TERMINATED instance leads to teardown; Ctrl-C only stops watching for kernel-check modes; a reboot of the Mac leaves the VM running and the state file intact. The stale-heartbeat rule needs three consecutive fetched heartbeats older than 30 minutes, and every step of the heartbeat loop is time-bounded.

Disk: about 139 GB of 200 GB (7.7 compressed, 61.6 unpacked, 68.7 swap, small files). The dd-written swap file has no holes, which XFS swap needs. Core dumps are off. The 300 MB/s disk is not a bottleneck: the parsers read at 35 to 170 MB/s and the file starts in page cache.

Steady-state memory: 82.6 + 98.8 GiB for the two kernels plus the parent's remainder, against about 251 GiB and 64 GiB swap. The rule at line 482 allows a parent of up to 121.7 GiB resident with swap and 64.1 GiB without.

A deadline or timeout kill is recorded honestly: exit status 124 or 137, 'not_finished' or 'not_run', and no accept facts, because lake prints 'Your solution is okay!' only after every kernel has returned 0.

verification.overall:
Second review, lens money/time/lost results. Read-only; nothing touched the cloud, the bucket or the repository. I read <REPO>/cloud/gcp/kernel_guest.sh in full, the launch/watch/teardown code and the diff of <REPO>/cloud/gcp/pilot_local.sh, Lean v4.36.0 Check.lean / Compare.lean / Axioms.lean / LeanChecker.lean, bubblewrap 0.9.0, nanoda and con-ron at the pinned commits, the published logs and page, and the export-check record. I also fetched, as text only, curl 8.5.0 tool_operate.c, systemd v255 (service.c, cgroup.c, manager.c, man pages) and the GCE guest agent's startup-script unit and runner. My stand-in tests and fetched sources are under <SCRATCH>/verify_money/ (tests/pipe, tests/deadman, tests/frag, tests/patched; fetch_curl, fetch_systemd, fetch_guestagent).

Result: all eleven of the first reviewer's defects are real as mechanisms; none is a blocker, and I agree there is no path that records a checker as accepting when it did not run or failed. I re-rated by cost if it happens, discounted where the trigger is remote: two stay major (the rehearsal never runs the branch that starts the paranoid kernel; the 15 h deadline), the con-ron wait drops to minor (certain mechanism, needs a stalled connection), the out-of-memory item drops to minor (the trace is in comparator.err, which is uploaded). The rest are minor as reported. Two corrections to the first report: (1) the 1.11 speed ratio is against the published REBUILD machine; the page says the kernel runs were made on the original build machine, which it does not name, so that calibration is weaker than presented; a second calibration from con-leche's slowest single-theorem checks gives 0.94 to 1.26 with this machine type fully loaded, which makes the deadline risk small but not nil. (2) For the memory rule, use VmRSS+VmSwap for the parent but keep SwapTotal; switching to SwapFree as well counts the parent's swapped pages twice.

Two defects the first reviewer missed. (A, major) Nothing notices a main script that is hung outside the monitoring loop or has died: the deadline subshell only kills user chk's processes, and the heartbeat subshell keeps beating on its own, so `watch` sees a healthy guest until Google's limit (16 h, 32.07 USD, no kernel_facts.json, no power-off). full_guest.sh has a watchdog for this; kernel_guest.sh does not. Triggers: a stalled download in a foreground step with no time limit (line 213); a fatal shell error in a path the rehearsal does not reach; and, depending on which startup-script unit the image carries, any out-of-memory kill, because systemd's default OOMPolicy=stop then terminates the unit's main process (source-confirmed), and if that process is the one reading the script's output the script dies of SIGPIPE at its second next output line (reproduced with stand-ins). (B, minor) No run-twice guard, unlike full_guest.sh and pilot_guest.sh: a restart of the VM, more reachable now that it is left powered off rather than deleted, truncates facts.tsv and uploads a FAIL stub over a finished run's kernel_facts.json and status.

Cap arithmetic confirmed with bc and the ledger: 46.32 recorded, cap 100, worst cases 32.07 and 0.52, sum 78.91; widened limits (DEADLINE_MIN=1140, MAXRUN=72000) give 40.07 and 86.91. Could a passing rehearsal be followed by a first-hour failure: yes, from the unrehearsed detection branch and from lake comparator's own memory while it parses the 61.6 GB export; the statement comparison itself is not a risk (the published lake comparator run got past it on the same two files, same hashes, about 30 minutes in). Cheaper way: I agree there is none that is material; one kernel at a time on a 128 GB machine comes to about 23 USD against about 24.6, with 23 hours of wall time and less memory headroom.

Fix before launch, in this order: extend the rehearsal to run the detection branch; widen the deadline (free unless used); add the dead-man heartbeat, deadline watchdog and time limits; correct the power-off statement. All my replacement lines were applied to a scratch copy that passes bash -n (tests/patched/kernel_guest.patched.sh); none has run on a real machine.

new_defects.scenario: Nothing notices a main script that is hung outside the monitoring loop or has died. Line 160 (`sleep ...; touch "$PD/DEADLINE"; pkill -KILL -u chk`) only kills user chk's processes and sets a marker that only the loop at line 471 reads; the heartbeat above runs on its own. So the status stays RUNNING, the heartbeat stays fresh, `watch` has no rule that fires, there is no finish, no kernel_facts.json and no power-off, and the VM runs to Google's limit: 16 h, 32.07 USD. full_guest.sh has a watchdog that takes over in this case; this script has none. Three ways in. (1) A stalled download in a foreground step with no time limit: line 213 (`curl -sSf .../elan-init.sh | sh`, and the curl inside elan-init.sh) has neither --max-time nor a speed limit, and the process is root's, so the deadline's pkill does not touch it. Elan's own toolchain download is bounded (30 s at under 10 B/s, elan src/download/src/lib.rs 183-191). (2) The main script dies. Any fatal shell error does it (an unbound variable under `set -u` in a path the rehearsal does not reach). So may any out-of-memory kill: systemd's default OOMPolicy is stop (v255 manager.c 4975), and for a oneshot service still in its start phase it sends SIGTERM to the unit's main process (service.c 3648-3671) when a process in the unit's cgroup is killed for memory (cgroup.c 3457-3485); the checkers are in that cgroup, since runuser does not move them. If that main process is the one reading the script's output (google_metadata_script_runner run directly; its runCmd has no signal handler), `tee` dies on its next write and the script dies of SIGPIPE at the output line after that, while the heartbeat goes on. I reproduced this chain with stand-ins (verify_money/tests/pipe: after the reader was sent TERM the main loop died within two lines and the heartbeat was still fresh). On the guest agent's current main branch the unit starts a bash adapter that starts the runner as a child, and with KillMode=process only the adapter is killed, so the script would survive; which unit this image carries I could not establish. How sure: the gap is certain from the code; trigger (1) is a remote network event; the out-of-memory route depends on the image and on memory running out, which the estimates do not predict.

verification.overall:
Both reported defects are real, and neither is a bug in the launcher diff itself. I agree with the first reviewer that the two new modes launch, watch and tear down correctly. I did not run the launcher, gcloud or test_spot_launcher.sh; my checks were source reading, two small bash 3.2 stand-in tests, and a scan of the local copy of the challenge export.

- **L1 (major):** the rehearsal cannot reach kernel_guest.sh lines 475-493, the code that decides whether the 10-hour paranoid kernel starts. I found no bug in those lines by reading; the problem is that they first run about an hour into the $2/h run. A three-line fix makes the rehearsal exercise them. Its pieces pass a local stand-in test and a check against the real challenge export, but the fix has not run on a VM.
- **L2 (minor):** the guest's self-poweroff cancels Google's scheduled deletion, while the launcher and guest text say deletion happens "whatever happens". The fix is wording only; the poweroff itself is the cheaper behaviour.
- **N1 (new, minor):** `launch kernel-check` does not check that the proof's export is already kept in the bucket. If it is not, the $2/h machine fetches 7.7 GB from the published site, with a worst case of 7.5 hours (about $15) before FAIL. One launcher line closes it.

The three doubts:
- **Time budget:** probably fits, with 1 to 2.7 hours of slack. The repo's own records put this machine 11-26% slower per thread than the published one; the paranoid kernel is killed only beyond about 36% slower.
- **Kept export:** confirmed as read, and raised to N1.
- **n4d-highmem-4:** exists (4 vCPUs, 32 GB) per Google's machine-type page, fetched today.

Other points I re-checked and agree with:
- `/bin/bash -n` passes under 3.2.57 for both scripts.
- The facts one-liner returns the two recorded hashes from the real export_facts.json and refuses four damaged variants.
- The local copy of challenge.ndjson.zst unpacks (`--long=27`) to 350,862,311 bytes with SHA-256 bd484ac9…, the value the guest will insist on.
- The real ledger holds $46.32 with no open row and no state file, so the cap allows kernel-check's $32.07 worst case.
- con-ron at the pinned commit accepts `--`, `--compare`, `--progress=` and `--jobs=`.
- test_spot_launcher.sh launches none of the new modes.
